correctness.rationale: The proof starts from fixed Taft relations and coproduct and reconstructs all coefficients of \(\Psi_2(x^rg^b)\) by the quantum binomial recurrence. It derives an exact unitary Fourier–Hankel block factorization; Fourier vectors give all \(n^2\) singular values including zeros. It proves the even/odd first-layer singular profiles via disjoint column pairing or a weighted cyclic shift with trivial monodromy. The original verification program, read from its actual packaged source, independently checks coproduct expansion for \(2\le n\le8\) and all-block factorization/SVD for \(2\le n\le12\). Finite tests are acknowledged as corroboration only. No unsupported higher-block nonvanishing or gauge invariance is asserted.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant original Taft construction, full Taft-indicator section, and relevant connected-graded Adams-operator primary theorems were inspected for actual implication. The closest results concern antipode order, trace/indicators, or connected-case eigenvalues, and do not cover the Taft Hopf-square SVD. Independent searches for matrix aliases, quantum-binomial Hankel spectra and first-layer parity gave no directly covering published claim. Absence of matching records is not a proof of global novelty; a specialized unlocated equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: A more specialized treatment of Taft Hopf-power matrix Fourier transforms or singular values outside the inspected primary works could already imply the formulas.
The metric is a chosen PBW-orthonormal normalization, so the result is not a categorical invariant; this is a scope limitation, not an originality claim.
The original 1971 Taft publication supplies only a month-resolution publication date in primary bibliographic records; it is not assigned a guessed calendar day.

value.rationale: Nonsemisimple Taft algebras and their Sweedler powers are established natural objects. Complete singular-value data provide rank/conditioning information absent from scalar higher indicators or eigenvalue-only classifications. The all-degree formula is a nontrivial explicit unitary reduction from \(n^2\)-dimensional Hopf square to cyclic Fourier sums, and the first nontrivial nilpotent layer reveals an exact even–odd stability transition: condition number \(1\) versus \(\csc(\pi/(2n))\sim2n/\pi\). The result is meaningful within the explicitly fixed PBW metric and does not claim unavailable categorical invariance.
